### White Boy Rick — Crime, Family & Betrayal

White Boy Rick (2018) tells the true story of Richard Wershe Jr., a teenager growing up in 1980s Detroit who becomes involved in the dangerous world of drug trafficking while secretly working as an informant for the FBI.

Living in a struggling neighborhood, Rick is drawn into the drug trade at a young age. His connections and growing reputation attract the attention of federal agents, who recruit him to gather information about local dealers and criminal organizations. Caught between law enforcement and the streets, Rick begins living two lives that become increasingly difficult to separate.

As Rick becomes more deeply involved, the risks grow beyond anything he initially understands. His relationship with his family is tested, while the people who once relied on him begin to see him as a threat. Eventually, the decisions made by both Rick and the authorities lead him toward consequences that will change his life forever.

The film explores themes of poverty, family loyalty, corruption, exploitation, and the consequences of youthful decisions. It also raises questions about the responsibilities of law enforcement when a teenager becomes entangled in an adult world of crime.

What makes White Boy Rick compelling is the tragic transformation of a young boy who becomes caught between the criminal world and the very authorities who recruited him.

💬 He was just a teenager caught between the streets and the system—and both came at a price.

source_details.synopsis: White Boy Rick is a 2018 American crime drama film directed by Yann Demange and written by Andy Weiss, Logan Miller, and Noah Miller. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Richie Merritt in his film debut, Bel Powley, Jennifer Jason Leigh, Brian Tyree Henry, Rory Cochrane, RJ Cyler, Jonathan Majors, Eddie Marsan, Bruce Dern, and Piper Laurie in her final film role. The film is loosely based on the story of Richard Wershe Jr., who in the 1980s became the youngest FBI informant ever at the age of 14.
